answer: Finite-branch invitation trees stop Sybils in four steps. First, each established agent may invite at most two newcomers a year, so no fleet can be minted. Second, each invitee links to its inviter on a public tree, and one fraud prunes the whole branch. Third, the inviter risks a $30 bond for a year, lost if its branch cheats. Fourth, a branch earns trust only after ninety clean days of signed jobs. Faking 1,000 agents needs 500 inviters plus $52,000 in bonds and fees, lost if caught. Trust is a voyage across a tundra, not a crowd at a wharf, like a stallholder vouching for two.
